scenarios.title: Repair a services file and replace stale router rules
scenarios.summary: Diagnose a correct-looking name that still selects obsolete router permits; restore TCP and UDP without opening unrelated traffic.
scenarios.objective: Save only these lookup meanings: report/tcp and reports/tcp select port 7443; report/udp and reports/udp select port 8853; clock/udp and time/udp select port 123. Comments, spacing, row order and canonical/alias choice may differ. Permit outgoing TCP/7443 and UDP/8853 from LAN fd66:70:80::/64 on lan0 toward 2001:db8:180::/64 through wan0 in NEW and ESTABLISHED contexts. Permit their reverse traffic only in ESTABLISHED context with the matching service source port. Replace the obsolete numeric permits: saving a mapping alone does not update installed rules. Block other TCP/UDP, including old ports, crossed protocol numbers, unsolicited arrivals and wrong ranges/directions. All addresses in the stated ranges must work, not only displayed samples. Keep incoming ICMPv6 type 2, code 0 from wan0 to that LAN through lan0; block other modeled ICMPv6 headers. Keep supplied INPUT/OUTPUT, forwarding, routes and interfaces unchanged. Use Check work after saving the file and repairing the current policy. Equivalent supported names, aliases, numeric ports and rule arrangements are accepted; editing either workspace invalidates old feedback.
scenarios.retry_guidance: Compare the saved getent result with ip6tables -S. Save repairs before creating a new named rule; inspect both transports and their reverse directions.
steps: Repair the saved mappings and installed permits

guide.title: Repair the example mapping
guide.why: cat /etc/services shows the simulated saved file. getent services previews/tcp asks for the TCP meaning of that alias; /udp asks separately. A successful lookup proves a mapping exists, not that a server is running or traffic can pass. The supplied listener ports are the task facts.
guide.action: The example listeners use preview/tcp 9443 and preview/udp 9553, both with alias previews. In the editor, repair those two entries, keep clock and time at 123/udp, then choose Save virtual file.

commands.explanation: Read the actual saved example file, separate from unsaved editor text.
Look up the saved TCP alias; compare its actual number with the example listener at 9443.
Look up the UDP meaning separately; its example listener uses 9553.
Inspect the numeric rules already installed; saving a name does not reload them.

guide.title: Compare the lookup with installed rules
guide.why: When a named ip6tables port is used, the simulator resolves it when creating the rule and stores the number. After saving a repaired file, ip6tables -S can still show the obsolete number. Replace the affected permit; new rule creation then uses the saved mapping. A numeric port is also a valid solution when the required file meanings are correct.
guide.action: Choose getent services previews/tcp, Insert command, then Run command; repeat with /udp. Run ip6tables -S and compare the stored port numbers. Replace the obsolete permits using the separate worked sequence if needed.

guide.title: Test the repair and its boundaries
guide.why: Run both TCP and UDP request/reply tests, then test old and crossed ports and unsolicited traffic. A reverse permit needs ESTABLISHED, the reversed prefixes and the service source port. Preserve the selected control header. Check example compares the entire stated address and port ranges as well as the samples; it does not prove a real application or TCP handshake.
guide.action: Run TCP request, reply and follow-up, then the UDP test. Test old/crossed ports, unsolicited arrivals and the selected control header. Choose Check example after the repair.

scenarios.explanation: The saved services file chooses a port for each transport; it does not control an already stored match. Repair the TCP and UDP meanings, recreate permits with the intended numbers, then verify requests, actual replies and refusal cases. The whole-range checks also protect unlisted clients and unwanted ports. Numeric rules and equivalent supported file formatting are valid when all required meanings and outcomes hold.
hints: Read cat /etc/services and both protocol-specific getent results; the TCP and UDP listeners have different supplied ports.
A saved edit does not change old rules. Inspect numeric -S output and replace obsolete source- and destination-port matches.
Keep full LAN/remote prefixes and explicit directions. Outgoing rules allow NEW and ESTABLISHED; reverse rules allow ESTABLISHED only. Preserve the selected control header.
scenarios.simplifications: All file text, numeric rules and TCP/UDP direction events are virtual and bounded. Only the saved supplied services file is consulted, not host NSS or /etc/services. The strict file subset rejects duplicate names/aliases or port/protocol entries. No running server, real packet, TCP handshake, ICMP RELATED association, IPv6 NAT or production firewall completeness is modeled. Routes, local chains and forwarding are supplied. Editing and saving progress are not Linux boot persistence.
